Research interests
My research interests center on causal inference and applied econometrics, particularly difference-in-differences designs, panel and longitudinal data analysis, and combining NLP/machine-learning methods with causal statistical inference to study questions in economics and technology (e.g., algorithmic amplification and content bias on social media platforms).

title: Alexandra Gamez
text:
Selected projects

Algorithmic Amplification & Content Bias on Twitter/X — Built an end-to-end research pipeline (data collection, an NLP/ML classification system, and causal inference) to estimate the effect of a major platform policy change on content visibility using a difference-in-differences design with a matched control group, applied to a 4-year, ~695,000-observation dataset.
Wages vs. Inflation: A CPI Analysis — Built a Python pipeline to collect, clean, merge, and validate BLS and FRED time-series data into a longitudinal panel, with descriptive statistics and visualizations of real vs. nominal wage trends.
